full_judgment: 2. Appellant filed Misc. Case No. 43 of 1976 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 against respondents on 1-4-76 for pre-emption of 1.60 acres of land in which the appellant is a co-sharer out of 1.89 acres of land sold by respondent No. 2 (Vendor opposite party No. 7) to the respondent No. 1 (purchaser O.P. No. 2) on 10-1-76. The main case of the appellant was that he was a co-sharer in the case holding and the respondent No. 1 was a stranger : that no notice of sale was either issued or served on the appellant; that the appellant came to know of the sale after obtaining certified copy on hearing about the sale. The respondent No. 2 i.e. Vendor though filed written objection stating that by two sale deeds dated 22-2-76 and 23-2-76 the purchaser respondent No. 1 had reconveyed the case land to her but she did not contest the case. It was contested by the purchaser respondent No. 1 mainly on the ground that since land had been reconveyed by two registered sale deeds dated 22-2-76 and 23-2-76 on receipt of consideration and therefore the prayer for pre-emption was not maintainable.
